current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents ac input amplitude for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Retain the stated strain-sensing scope. Record voltage versus current and the amplitude convention for each value; do not convert between conventions without the waveform information.
rationale: The previous definition merely repeated the label and omitted the strain-sensing context.
recommended_value: Magnitude of the sinusoidal electrical excitation applied when acquiring an impedance-based strain-sensing signal, with the excitation quantity identified as voltage or current and the amplitude convention identified as peak, peak-to-peak, or root-mean-square.
registry_final_value: Magnitude of the sinusoidal electrical excitation applied when acquiring an impedance-based strain-sensing signal, with the excitation quantity identified as voltage or current and the amplitude convention identified as peak, peak-to-peak, or root-mean-square.
released_value: Magnitude of the sinusoidal electrical excitation applied when acquiring an impedance-based strain-sensing signal, with the excitation quantity identified as voltage or current and the amplitude convention identified as peak, peak-to-peak, or root-mean-square.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents activated sludge volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Identify the activated-sludge suspension and the mixture components. If the experimental denominator was final measured mixture volume, retain that protocol-specific volume-concentration convention explicitly instead.
rationale: This is a mixture-composition percentage, not a spatial dimension.  References 22.
recommended_value: Percentage of the preparation volume represented by activated-sludge inoculum, calculated as its added volume divided by the sum of the component volumes before mixing and multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: Percentage of the preparation volume represented by activated-sludge inoculum, calculated as its added volume divided by the sum of the component volumes before mixing and multiplied by 100.
released_value: Percentage of the preparation volume represented by activated-sludge inoculum, calculated as its added volume divided by the sum of the component volumes before mixing and multiplied by 100.

current_value: A scan-rate characteristic specifying the spatial or linewise rate at which an atomic-force-microscopy probe traverses a specimen during acquisition.
implementation: Use this definition for length/time records. For records reported in hertz, use the alternative below as a separately labelled AFM line scan frequency; remove the line-rate alias from the speed class.
rationale: Linear scan speed and raster line repetition frequency have different dimensions; the existing definition combines them.  References 42.
recommended_value: Linear speed of the atomic-force-microscopy probe relative to the specimen along the scan trajectory.
registry_final_value: A scan-rate characteristic specifying the spatial or linewise rate at which an atomic-force-microscopy probe traverses a specimen during acquisition.
released_value: A scan-rate characteristic specifying the spatial or linewise rate at which an atomic-force-microscopy probe traverses a specimen during acquisition.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents aggregate aspect ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State whether the dimensions are fitted ellipsoid axes, Feret diameters, or another measure. A spherical aggregate has ratio 1; retain any source using the reciprocal as a separate convention.
rationale: An aspect ratio describes shape, not chemical composition.
recommended_value: Ratio of an aggregate’s major characteristic dimension to its minor characteristic dimension, evaluated using the same specified shape-fitting or image-analysis convention.
registry_final_value: Ratio of an aggregate’s major characteristic dimension to its minor characteristic dimension, evaluated using the same specified shape-fitting or image-analysis convention.
released_value: Ratio of an aggregate’s major characteristic dimension to its minor characteristic dimension, evaluated using the same specified shape-fitting or image-analysis convention.

current_value: A density characteristic that represents ag nw surface density for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Count per area and projected area coverage are different quantities and should not be stored under this definition.
rationale: The areal-loading description and mass-per-area alias support a mass surface density.
recommended_value: Mass of deposited silver nanowires divided by the coated substrate area.
registry_final_value: Mass of deposited silver nanowires divided by the coated substrate area.
released_value: Mass of deposited silver nanowires divided by the coated substrate area.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ag nw weight fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use this replacement for dry-total-solids fractions. Check the source recipe: if the reference is polymer mass alone, use the alternative and rename the class Silver-nanowire-to-polymer mass ratio. Do not reinterpret existing percentages without checking their denominator.
rationale: A mass fraction requires a whole-mixture denominator; a nanowire-to-polymer ratio is a different quantity.  References 18.
recommended_value: Mass of silver nanowires divided by the combined dry mass of all constituents of the nanocomposite.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents ag nw weight fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents ag nw weight fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A transport characteristic that represents air diffusion layer thickness fraction in mcl for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm that MCL denotes the source multilayer cathode and that its layer Z is the air-diffusion sublayer; express as a fraction or multiply by 100 for a percentage.
rationale: This is a geometric thickness ratio even when it influences gas transport.
recommended_value: Through-plane thickness of the air-diffusion sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the multilayer cathode containing it.
registry_final_value: Through-plane thickness of the air-diffusion sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the multilayer cathode containing it.
released_value: Through-plane thickness of the air-diffusion sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the multilayer cathode containing it.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents aluminum nitrate solution volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: The numerator is the stock solution, not the volume of dissolved aluminum nitrate. Record the stock concentration. If the source uses added stock volume divided by ferritin-solution volume alone, rename that quantity as a stock-solution-to-ferritin-solution volume ratio.
rationale: The term denotes a formulation composition fraction rather than geometric size.  References 22.
recommended_value: Volume of the aluminum-nitrate stock solution added during preparation divided by the sum of all liquid-component volumes before mixing.
registry_final_value: Volume of the aluminum-nitrate stock solution added during preparation divided by the sum of all liquid-component volumes before mixing.
released_value: Volume of the aluminum-nitrate stock solution added during preparation divided by the sum of all liquid-component volumes before mixing.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents ammonium carbonate solution concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Record the chemical formula, solution conditions, and concentration unit; this is not the final ammonium carbonate concentration after dilution into ink.
rationale: The description identifies a molar concentration; the replacement makes the amount and solution-volume basis explicit.  References 14.
recommended_value: Amount of ammonium carbonate solute divided by the volume of the prepared ammonium-carbonate solution.
registry_final_value: Amount of ammonium carbonate solute divided by the volume of the prepared ammonium-carbonate solution.
released_value: Amount of ammonium carbonate solute divided by the volume of the prepared ammonium-carbonate solution.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents anode catalyst loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Identify the numerator in each record, for example platinum mass, palladium mass, or total supported-catalyst powder mass. If homogeneous quantities are needed, represent these as distinct subclasses; do not change historical metal loadings into powder loadings.
rationale: The replacement defines the area normalization without treating catalytic-metal mass and whole supported-powder mass as identical.
recommended_value: Mass of the specified catalyst material in the anode divided by the geometric electrode area over which that material is deposited.
registry_final_value: Mass of the specified catalyst material in the anode divided by the geometric electrode area over which that material is deposited.
released_value: Mass of the specified catalyst material in the anode divided by the geometric electrode area over which that material is deposited.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents anode mpl carbon support loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Exclude binder and other noncarbon constituents from the numerator; identify the actual MPL carbon material.
rationale: The areal carbon loading requires the carbon numerator and coated-area denominator.
recommended_value: Mass of carbon material in the anode microporous layer divided by the geometric area coated by that microporous layer.
registry_final_value: Mass of carbon material in the anode microporous layer divided by the geometric area coated by that microporous layer.
released_value: Mass of carbon material in the anode microporous layer divided by the geometric area coated by that microporous layer.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents anode stoichiometric ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: I is cell current and F is the Faraday constant. For a stack, state whether supply is per cell or stack-total; the denominator must use the same boundary. The ratio is undefined at zero consumption unless a reference-current convention is declared.
rationale: Reactant excess relative to consumption is an operating ratio, not the composition of the feed stream.
recommended_value: Ratio of the molar hydrogen supply rate to the anode to the stoichiometric hydrogen-consumption rate corresponding to the operating current; for a single hydrogen fuel cell the latter is I/(2F).
registry_final_value: Ratio of the molar hydrogen supply rate to the anode to the stoichiometric hydrogen-consumption rate corresponding to the operating current; for a single hydrogen fuel cell the latter is I/(2F).
released_value: Ratio of the molar hydrogen supply rate to the anode to the stoichiometric hydrogen-consumption rate corresponding to the operating current; for a single hydrogen fuel cell the latter is I/(2F).

current_value: A property denoting apparent density measured by helium pycnometry on fragments.
implementation: Rename the preferred label to Helium skeletal density if this is the intended measurement. Preserve the IRI only if it has consistently denoted this helium-derived quantity. If apparent density is intended as a broader concept, create a distinct skeletal-density term and retain apparent density only with an explicit envelope-volume convention.
rationale: The stated helium-pycnometry method supports skeletal density rather than an unspecified apparent or envelope density.  References 50.
recommended_value: Mass of a specimen divided by its helium-displaced volume, which excludes pores accessible to helium under the measurement conditions and includes solid material and helium-inaccessible pore volume.
registry_final_value: A property denoting apparent density measured by helium pycnometry on fragments.
released_value: A property denoting apparent density measured by helium pycnometry on fragments.

current_value: A property denoting backbone attachment molar percent and determined in Ionomer Coating Simulation.
implementation: This source-specific definition applies to the fluorinated polymer model. State the distance or contact criterion, simulation region, and time averaging. Do not apply it unchanged to a hydrocarbon polymer lacking fluorine.
rationale: The existing alias identifies the counted atoms; the replacement states the denominator and contact classification.
recommended_value: Percentage of the polymer-backbone fluorine atoms classified as attached to the graphite surface, calculated as the number of such attached atoms divided by the total number of backbone fluorine atoms and multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: Percentage of the polymer-backbone fluorine atoms classified as attached to the graphite surface, calculated as the number of such attached atoms divided by the total number of backbone fluorine atoms and multiplied by 100.
released_value: Percentage of the polymer-backbone fluorine atoms classified as attached to the graphite surface, calculated as the number of such attached atoms divided by the total number of backbone fluorine atoms and multiplied by 100.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents bath solute volume concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: For stock solutions, identify the stock composition; this is not the volume concentration of the pure dissolved substance. If the source uses pre-addition bath volume, preserve that denominator in a separately specified formulation ratio.
rationale: A liquid-additive volume per bath volume describes composition rather than geometric extent.
recommended_value: Volume of a specified liquid additive introduced into a plating bath divided by the volume of the prepared bath.
registry_final_value: Volume of a specified liquid additive introduced into a plating bath divided by the volume of the prepared bath.
released_value: Volume of a specified liquid additive introduced into a plating bath divided by the volume of the prepared bath.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents binder mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use the solvent-free solids basis. A binder-to-catalyst mass ratio is a separate quantity.
rationale: The description specifies a total-solids mass fraction; the replacement states that denominator.  References 18.
recommended_value: Mass of polymer binder divided by the total dry mass of all solids in the catalyst-layer formulation, including the binder.
registry_final_value: Mass of polymer binder divided by the total dry mass of all solids in the catalyst-layer formulation, including the binder.
released_value: Mass of polymer binder divided by the total dry mass of all solids in the catalyst-layer formulation, including the binder.

current_value: A property denoting binder mass loss fraction and determined in Thermogravimetric Analysis Measurement.
implementation: Use this definition only if the source normalizes to initial binder mass. If the reported TGA fraction is loss per initial composite mass, use the alternative and label it Binder-associated specimen mass-loss fraction. Record interval and atmosphere; subtract other contributions only when supported by the analysis.
rationale: Normalizing binder loss to binder mass measures binder loss fraction, whereas normalization to the entire specimen measures a different fraction.
recommended_value: Mass lost and assigned to binder decomposition during a specified thermogravimetric interval divided by the binder mass present before that interval.
registry_final_value: A property denoting binder mass loss fraction and determined in Thermogravimetric Analysis Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting binder mass loss fraction and determined in Thermogravimetric Analysis Measurement.

current_value: A temporal characteristic that represents bulk sedimentation time for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Specify the transmission criterion, observation position, centrifugal acceleration, and temperature. Use the source endpoint rather than introducing an arbitrary percentage.
rationale: An endpoint must distinguish onset, substantial separation, and completion.
recommended_value: Elapsed time from the start of an analytical-centrifugation test to a declared bulk-sedimentation or phase-separation endpoint identified from the recorded transmission profiles.
registry_final_value: Elapsed time from the start of an analytical-centrifugation test to a declared bulk-sedimentation or phase-separation endpoint identified from the recorded transmission profiles.
released_value: Elapsed time from the start of an analytical-centrifugation test to a declared bulk-sedimentation or phase-separation endpoint identified from the recorded transmission profiles.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents carbon black volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State whether the representative volume includes pore space and whether a supported-catalyst particle is segmented into carbon and metal. If the original model instead normalizes to solids volume only, use that explicitly labelled solid-phase fraction.
rationale: A constituent volume fraction is compositional; the replacement supplies the modeled system denominator.  References 15.
recommended_value: Volume occupied by the carbon-black solid phase divided by the total representative catalyst-layer volume used in the stated microstructure model.
registry_final_value: Volume occupied by the carbon-black solid phase divided by the total representative catalyst-layer volume used in the stated microstructure model.
released_value: Volume occupied by the carbon-black solid phase divided by the total representative catalyst-layer volume used in the stated microstructure model.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents carbon dioxide percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm the source uses volume percent. If it uses amount percent, label that basis explicitly; the two coincide for an ideal gas mixture but need not be silently conflated in all conditions.
rationale: The incubator context supports a gas-composition percentage rather than an unspecified percentage.
recommended_value: Percentage of carbon dioxide in the incubator atmosphere, defined as its gas volume divided by total gas volume at the same temperature and pressure and multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents carbon dioxide percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents carbon dioxide percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents carbon monoxide volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Record wet or dry gas basis where relevant.
rationale: The quantity describes gas composition, not geometry.
recommended_value: Carbon-monoxide gas volume divided by the total volume of the carbon-monoxide/nitrogen feed mixture, evaluated at the same temperature and pressure and multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: Carbon-monoxide gas volume divided by the total volume of the carbon-monoxide/nitrogen feed mixture, evaluated at the same temperature and pressure and multiplied by 100.
released_value: Carbon-monoxide gas volume divided by the total volume of the carbon-monoxide/nitrogen feed mixture, evaluated at the same temperature and pressure and multiplied by 100.

current_value: A property denoting carbon weight percent in catalyst.
implementation: Use this replacement if catalyst denotes the supported powder. If the data refer to a complete layer containing ionomer and other solids, create or use a layer-specific carbon mass percentage instead.
rationale: This distinguishes carbon content in a catalyst powder from carbon content in an entire formulated catalyst layer.  References 18.
recommended_value: Mass of carbon in a dry supported-catalyst material divided by the total dry mass of that catalyst material and multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: A property denoting carbon weight percent in catalyst.
released_value: A property denoting carbon weight percent in catalyst.

current_value: A property denoting carbon yield (mass retained after pyrolysis) attributed to lignin content; referenced qualitatively and via TGA/porosity discussion (not tabulated).
implementation: State pyrolysis temperature, atmosphere, and duration. This is char/residue yield; do not call it elemental-carbon yield unless elemental analysis supports that interpretation.
rationale: A yield requires a reference amount; a residue mass alone is not a yield.
recommended_value: Mass of the carbonaceous residue remaining after a specified pyrolysis treatment divided by the initial dry precursor mass, expressed as a fraction or percentage.
registry_final_value: Mass of the carbonaceous residue remaining after a specified pyrolysis treatment divided by the initial dry precursor mass, expressed as a fraction or percentage.
released_value: Mass of the carbonaceous residue remaining after a specified pyrolysis treatment divided by the initial dry precursor mass, expressed as a fraction or percentage.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents carrier gas flow for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use quantity-kind subclasses or an explicit basis field. For volumetric flow, state actual or standard reference temperature and pressure; do not mix flow rate with gas velocity.
rationale: The replacement defines a flow-rate family while retaining the physical basis required for each value.
recommended_value: Rate at which an identified carrier gas is supplied through the specified process boundary, expressed on a declared volumetric, amount-of-substance, or mass basis.
registry_final_value: Rate at which an identified carrier gas is supplied through the specified process boundary, expressed on a declared volumetric, amount-of-substance, or mass basis.
released_value: Rate at which an identified carrier gas is supplied through the specified process boundary, expressed on a declared volumetric, amount-of-substance, or mass basis.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst and ionomer to peg ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm the source recipe uses a mass ratio before adopting this definition. Identify the catalyst material and dry ionomer mass; exclude dispersion solvent. If a different basis was used, preserve it as a separately defined ratio.
rationale: The components and ratio direction are clear, but the source does not explicitly establish the mass basis.
recommended_value: Combined dry mass of catalyst material and ionomer divided by the mass of polyethylene glycol additive used in the same formulation.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst and ionomer to peg ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst and ionomer to peg ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A morphological characteristic that represents catalyst layer tortuosity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Specify path-selection and averaging rules. Do not substitute the square of this ratio or a factor inferred from effective diffusivity; retain those as separately defined transport quantities.
rationale: The geometric-tortuosity aliases support a path-length ratio rather than a transport tortuosity factor.
recommended_value: Ratio of a specified mean connected path length through the catalyst-layer pore network to the straight through-layer distance in the selected direction.
registry_final_value: Ratio of a specified mean connected path length through the catalyst-layer pore network to the straight through-layer distance in the selected direction.
released_value: Ratio of a specified mean connected path length through the catalyst-layer pore network to the straight through-layer distance in the selected direction.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Identify numerator material for every value. Platinum-only loading and total Pt/C powder loading require separate quantity records or subclasses; a generic catalyst-loading parent may group them.
rationale: This specifies the areal basis while keeping metal mass and total supported-catalyst mass distinguishable.
recommended_value: Mass of an explicitly identified catalyst component deposited in an electrode divided by the geometric electrode area carrying that component.
registry_final_value: Mass of an explicitly identified catalyst component deposited in an electrode divided by the geometric electrode area carrying that component.
released_value: Mass of an explicitly identified catalyst component deposited in an electrode divided by the geometric electrode area carrying that component.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst loading pattern for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Describe segment positions and hydrophilic/hydrophobic treatment where applicable; represent numeric local loading separately.
rationale: The source pattern examples describe spatial categories rather than a constituent amount.
recommended_value: Categorical description of the spatial arrangement of deposited catalyst within an electrode, including a continuous full-area coating or a specified arrangement of coated and uncoated segments.
registry_final_value: Categorical description of the spatial arrangement of deposited catalyst within an electrode, including a continuous full-area coating or a specified arrangement of coated and uncoated segments.
released_value: Categorical description of the spatial arrangement of deposited catalyst within an electrode, including a continuous full-area coating or a specified arrangement of coated and uncoated segments.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic representing Catalyst Mass in the H2KG domain model.
implementation: A generic catalyst-mass class can remain broad. Identify the catalyst material in the value record; split metal-only and total supported-catalyst bases when homogeneous normalization is required. The Pt-mass alias issue is separate from definition acceptance.
rationale: The replacement identifies the material boundary without treating metal-only mass as synonymous with total supported-powder mass.
recommended_value: Mass of the identified catalyst material used as a specimen quantity or normalization basis, excluding separately added ionomer and solvent unless these are explicitly part of the identified material.
registry_final_value: Mass of the identified catalyst material used as a specimen quantity or normalization basis, excluding separately added ionomer and solvent unless these are explicitly part of the identified material.
released_value: Mass of the identified catalyst material used as a specimen quantity or normalization basis, excluding separately added ionomer and solvent unless these are explicitly part of the identified material.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst mass concentration in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use this definition only for records based on final ink volume. For the stated mg/mL of solvent convention, use the alternative and rename the quantity Catalyst mass per added solvent volume; existing values must not be silently reassigned between the two bases.
rationale: Standard mass concentration uses final mixture volume, whereas the description states catalyst mass per solvent volume.  References 17.
recommended_value: Mass of the identified dry catalyst material divided by the final volume of the prepared catalyst ink.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst mass concentration in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst mass concentration in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst suspension concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm the source uses mass concentration before adopting. A particle-number concentration or amount concentration must be defined separately; identify the catalyst and final suspension medium.
rationale: A heterogeneous catalyst suspension is commonly characterized on a mass-per-volume basis, but this source does not fix the concentration kind.  References 17.
recommended_value: Mass of the identified dry catalyst material divided by the final volume of its suspension.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst suspension concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst suspension concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst to nafion weight ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Identify which solids are counted as catalyst in the CoTMPP-based recipe. Nafion-to-carbon ratio and its abbreviation N/C are different quantities and should be removed as synonyms of this class.
rationale: The replacement fixes the stated catalyst-to-ionomer direction and excludes dispersion solvent from the polymer mass.
recommended_value: Dry mass of the catalyst material, including any additives that the source explicitly groups with it, divided by the dry mass of Nafion polymer in the same formulation.
registry_final_value: Dry mass of the catalyst material, including any additives that the source explicitly groups with it, divided by the dry mass of Nafion polymer in the same formulation.
released_value: Dry mass of the catalyst material, including any additives that the source explicitly groups with it, divided by the dry mass of Nafion polymer in the same formulation.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents catalyst weight percent in oil for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Rename the preferred label to Catalyst-to-oil mass percentage or Catalyst dosage relative to oil mass. If any records instead use catalyst divided by catalyst plus oil mass, keep them as a separate total-mixture mass fraction.
rationale: The description explicitly uses oil mass as the reference; this is an additive-to-feed mass percentage rather than catalyst mass fraction of the final mixture.
recommended_value: Mass of catalyst added to the reaction divided by the initial oil mass and multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: Mass of catalyst added to the reaction divided by the initial oil mass and multiplied by 100.
released_value: Mass of catalyst added to the reaction divided by the initial oil mass and multiplied by 100.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents cathode catalyst loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Identify the numerator in each record, for example platinum mass, palladium mass, or total supported-catalyst powder mass. If homogeneous quantities are needed, represent these as distinct subclasses; do not change historical metal loadings into powder loadings.
rationale: The replacement defines the area normalization without treating catalytic-metal mass and whole supported-powder mass as identical.
recommended_value: Mass of the specified catalyst material in the cathode divided by the geometric electrode area over which that material is deposited.
registry_final_value: Mass of the specified catalyst material in the cathode divided by the geometric electrode area over which that material is deposited.
released_value: Mass of the specified catalyst material in the cathode divided by the geometric electrode area over which that material is deposited.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents cathode mpl carbon support loading for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Exclude binder and other noncarbon constituents from the numerator; identify the actual MPL carbon material.
rationale: The areal carbon loading requires the carbon numerator and coated-area denominator.
recommended_value: Mass of carbon material in the cathode microporous layer divided by the geometric area coated by that microporous layer.
registry_final_value: Mass of carbon material in the cathode microporous layer divided by the geometric area coated by that microporous layer.
released_value: Mass of carbon material in the cathode microporous layer divided by the geometric area coated by that microporous layer.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents cathode stoichiometric ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: I is cell current and F is the Faraday constant. For air feed, calculate supplied oxygen from the air flow and its oxygen composition. State per-cell versus stack boundary and any reference-current convention at zero current.
rationale: The quantity compares reactant supply with reaction demand; it is not oxygen fraction in the feed.
recommended_value: Ratio of the molar oxygen supply rate to the cathode to the stoichiometric oxygen-consumption rate corresponding to the operating current; for a single hydrogen fuel cell the latter is I/(4F).
registry_final_value: Ratio of the molar oxygen supply rate to the cathode to the stoichiometric oxygen-consumption rate corresponding to the operating current; for a single hydrogen fuel cell the latter is I/(4F).
released_value: Ratio of the molar oxygen supply rate to the cathode to the stoichiometric oxygen-consumption rate corresponding to the operating current; for a single hydrogen fuel cell the latter is I/(4F).

current_value: A density characteristic that represents cell seeding density for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use this definition for cells-per-area records. If the source reports cells per suspension volume, use the alternative as a separately labelled cell-seeding number concentration.
rationale: Surface seeding density and suspension cell concentration have different dimensional bases.
recommended_value: Initial number of biological cells seeded onto a culture substrate divided by the seeded substrate area.
registry_final_value: A density characteristic that represents cell seeding density for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A density characteristic that represents cell seeding density for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A property denoting xPS-derived surface oxidation-state ratio for Co.
implementation: State the fitted spectral components and correction convention. Treat the result as an XPS-derived surface estimate rather than an unqualified bulk stoichiometric ratio.
rationale: The Co2+/Co3+ alias identifies the ratio direction that was absent from the primary definition.
recommended_value: Ratio of the estimated surface abundance of cobalt in oxidation state +2 to that in oxidation state +3, obtained from a declared X-ray photoelectron-spectroscopy peak-fitting model.
registry_final_value: Ratio of the estimated surface abundance of cobalt in oxidation state +2 to that in oxidation state +3, obtained from a declared X-ray photoelectron-spectroscopy peak-fitting model.
released_value: Ratio of the estimated surface abundance of cobalt in oxidation state +2 to that in oxidation state +3, obtained from a declared X-ray photoelectron-spectroscopy peak-fitting model.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents coagulating agent mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm whether the source includes PEI in total dry solids. If the denominator excludes the additive, use the alternative and label it Coagulating-agent-to-base-solids mass ratio.
rationale: The dry-solids basis must be distinguished from a wet-ink fraction and from additive mass relative to pre-existing solids.  References 18.
recommended_value: Mass of the coagulating additive divided by the total dry mass of all formulation solids, including that additive.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents coagulating agent mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents coagulating agent mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A property denoting constrictivity derived from reconstructed pore-network bottlenecks in FIBSEM Tomography Measurement.
implementation: Attach the actual equation and direction to each source-specific calculation. Do not interchange throat-to-body size ratios, squared ratios, or transport-based factors; create method-specific subclasses when numerical interoperability requires one formula.
rationale: This captures the physical concept without choosing among non-equivalent numerical constrictivity formulae.
recommended_value: Dimensionless descriptor of the restriction imposed by variations in pore cross-section, particularly constrictions connecting larger pore bodies, evaluated using a declared pore-network or transport model.
registry_final_value: Dimensionless descriptor of the restriction imposed by variations in pore cross-section, particularly constrictions connecting larger pore bodies, evaluated using a declared pore-network or transport model.
released_value: Dimensionless descriptor of the restriction imposed by variations in pore cross-section, particularly constrictions connecting larger pore bodies, evaluated using a declared pore-network or transport model.

current_value: A density characteristic that represents co stripping specific charge density for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State assumed CO coverage, catalyst surface, background treatment, and the adopted calibration value and unit. Do not insert a universal numerical value for all catalysts or adsorption protocols.
rationale: The calibration-charge alias supports a reference charge density rather than measured stripping charge per geometric area.
recommended_value: Reference oxidation charge per unit real platinum surface area assigned to removal of a specified adsorbed carbon-monoxide coverage during CO-stripping voltammetry, used to convert integrated stripping charge to electrochemically active platinum area.
registry_final_value: Reference oxidation charge per unit real platinum surface area assigned to removal of a specified adsorbed carbon-monoxide coverage during CO-stripping voltammetry, used to convert integrated stripping charge to electrochemically active platinum area.
released_value: Reference oxidation charge per unit real platinum surface area assigned to removal of a specified adsorbed carbon-monoxide coverage during CO-stripping voltammetry, used to convert integrated stripping charge to electrochemically active platinum area.

current_value: A property denoting CPE admittance Y 0 and determined in Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Potentiostatic and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Galvanostatic.
implementation: For omega in rad/s and unnormalized admittance in siemens, Y0 has units S s^n. Record n and whether the fitted element is normalized to area; Y0 equals capacitance only when n = 1.
rationale: Y0 is an admittance prefactor, not generally an ordinary conductance or capacitance.  References 34.
recommended_value: The frequency-independent coefficient multiplying the nth power of imaginary angular frequency in the admittance of a specified constant-phase element, where n is the element's dimensionless exponent.
registry_final_value: The frequency-independent coefficient multiplying the nth power of imaginary angular frequency in the admittance of a specified constant-phase element, where n is the element's dimensionless exponent.
released_value: The frequency-independent coefficient multiplying the nth power of imaginary angular frequency in the admittance of a specified constant-phase element, where n is the element's dimensionless exponent.

current_value: A property denoting crack aspect ratio and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.
implementation: Confirm the source uses length/width. If it uses aperture/length, depth/width, or another convention, replace the dimensions in the definition and retain that source-specific label.
rationale: A crack shape ratio is geometric, and its orientation must be stated to distinguish it from a reciprocal width-to-length ratio.
recommended_value: Ratio of a crack’s characteristic length to its characteristic width, using declared length and width extraction methods.
registry_final_value: A property denoting crack aspect ratio and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting crack aspect ratio and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents crack connectivity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Report as a fraction or percentage and state segmentation, connected-component, and crack-counting rules; record which interfaces define the layer thickness.
rationale: The description identifies a through-penetrating-crack count fraction rather than an unspecified connectivity metric.
recommended_value: Fraction of detected catalyst-layer cracks that span the complete layer thickness from one bounding interface to the other, calculated as the number of spanning cracks divided by the total number of detected cracks.
registry_final_value: Fraction of detected catalyst-layer cracks that span the complete layer thickness from one bounding interface to the other, calculated as the number of spanning cracks divided by the total number of detected cracks.
released_value: Fraction of detected catalyst-layer cracks that span the complete layer thickness from one bounding interface to the other, calculated as the number of spanning cracks divided by the total number of detected cracks.

current_value: A property denoting crack density and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.
implementation: Use this replacement only after confirming the source uses count per area. If it reports total crack length per area, use the first alternative and label Crack length density. If it reports area fraction, use the second alternative and label Crack area fraction.
rationale: Crack count per area, total crack length per area, and cracked-area fraction are distinct measures; the original does not identify one.
recommended_value: Number of individually identified cracks divided by the inspected specimen surface area.
registry_final_value: A property denoting crack density and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting crack density and determined in Crack Characterization Measurement.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack volume accessibility at 20 um for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm probe diameter before using this definition. If the source defines a 20-micrometre radius, use the alternative. State whether the algorithm includes the full intruded volume or only sphere-centre-accessible volume.
rationale: The source identifies probe-based accessible crack volume, but not whether 20 micrometres is the diameter or radius.
recommended_value: Fraction of the total segmented crack volume that a spherical probe of 20 micrometres diameter can reach from the membrane/catalyst-layer interface without intersecting the solid phase, under the stated simulated-intrusion algorithm.
registry_final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack volume accessibility at 20 um for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack volume accessibility at 20 um for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack width d 50 cwd for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State whether the cumulative distribution is number-, length-, area-, or volume-weighted and how local width is extracted. Remove mean crack width as a synonym unless the source itself incorrectly used that wording; preserve such source wording in provenance rather than the preferred scientific label.
rationale: D50 is a percentile, not a mean; its method and distribution basis must be retained.
recommended_value: Median of the crack-width distribution obtained by the declared crack-width-distribution image-analysis method, that is, the width at cumulative distribution fraction 0.5.
registry_final_value: Median of the crack-width distribution obtained by the declared crack-width-distribution image-analysis method, that is, the width at cumulative distribution fraction 0.5.
released_value: Median of the crack-width distribution obtained by the declared crack-width-distribution image-analysis method, that is, the width at cumulative distribution fraction 0.5.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents crack width d 50 mip for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State the size convention (diameter, radius, or aperture), cumulative weighting, interface of intrusion, and intrusion algorithm. Do not replace a source diameter with a radius or assume volume weighting without checking the source.
rationale: Intrusion-derived sizes are controlled by access constrictions and need not equal local geometric crack widths.
recommended_value: Median equivalent crack-entry size in the cumulative distribution generated by the declared simulated mercury-intrusion analysis, corresponding to cumulative fraction 0.5.
registry_final_value: Median equivalent crack-entry size in the cumulative distribution generated by the declared simulated mercury-intrusion analysis, corresponding to cumulative fraction 0.5.
released_value: Median equivalent crack-entry size in the cumulative distribution generated by the declared simulated mercury-intrusion analysis, corresponding to cumulative fraction 0.5.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents degree of sulfonation for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: For the stated sPEEK context, confirm the repeat-unit and proton-NMR integration convention. If the source defines a percentage of sulfonated sites instead, use the alternative with a site-based label and do not identify it numerically with groups per repeat unit without the conversion.
rationale: A group-per-repeat-unit degree must be distinguished from the fraction of available substitution sites that are occupied.
recommended_value: Average number of sulfonic-acid groups, including their ionized forms, attached per polymer repeat unit of an explicitly specified repeat-unit composition.
registry_final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents degree of sulfonation for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents degree of sulfonation for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents deposition rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Distinguish delivered volume from nominal syringe flow if losses or draw-out occur. Do not combine thickness-growth rate or deposited mass per time under this definition.
rationale: The description explicitly identifies a volumetric printing rate.
recommended_value: Volume of ink deposited onto or into the target structure per unit time during the specified printing process.
registry_final_value: VolumetricInkDepositionRate
released_value: Volume of ink deposited onto or into the target structure per unit time during the specified printing process.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents direct ink writing 2 for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Trace the original extracted field and source. If it represents a process, reuse the existing DirectInkWriting process class; if it represents a setting, recover its true name, quantity, and definition. Do not create a numerical definition or reclassify a setting as a process merely from the placeholder label.
rationale: This is an unresolved placeholder with no recoverable physical quantity.
registry_final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents direct ink writing 2 for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents direct ink writing 2 for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents dispersant mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm the source denominator. If dispersant is added relative to powder mass excluding dispersant, use the alternative and rename it Dispersant-to-powder mass ratio.
rationale: A dry-total-solids fraction differs from dispersant dosage relative to the ceramic powder alone.  References 18.
recommended_value: Mass of dispersant divided by the total dry mass of all solids in the ceramic ink, including the dispersant.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents dispersant mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents dispersant mass fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents dmso mass fraction in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use this only for total-ink mass fractions. If the reported 5 wt.% refers to the solvent mixture, use the alternative and rename the class DMSO mass fraction in solvent mixture. Confirm whether 5 wt.% denotes a fraction of the final mixture or an addition relative to an initial solvent amount.
rationale: The existing class label denotes whole-ink fraction whereas the description denotes solvent-mixture fraction.  References 18.
recommended_value: Mass of dimethyl sulfoxide divided by the total mass of the catalyst ink, including solvent and solids.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents dmso mass fraction in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents dmso mass fraction in ink for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A property denoting durability with cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.
implementation: State the cycling conditions, performance observable, baseline, and loss threshold. If the reported value is simply completed exposure without reaching an endpoint, use the alternative, rename it Cycling test duration, and record that the durability endpoint was not reached.
rationale: Durability expressed as time requires an endpoint; mere test exposure is not automatically a measured lifetime.
recommended_value: Elapsed operating time under a specified cycling protocol until a declared performance-loss or failure criterion is reached.
registry_final_value: A property denoting durability with cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting durability with cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.

current_value: A property denoting durability without cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.
implementation: State the noncycling conditions, performance observable, baseline, and loss threshold. If the reported value is simply completed exposure without reaching an endpoint, use the alternative, rename it Noncycling test duration, and record that the durability endpoint was not reached.
rationale: Durability expressed as time requires an endpoint; mere test exposure is not automatically a measured lifetime.
recommended_value: Elapsed operating time under a specified noncycling protocol until a declared performance-loss or failure criterion is reached.
registry_final_value: A property denoting durability without cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting durability without cycling hours and determined in MEA Durability Measurement.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents dye concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use this definition for mass/volume records. For molar records use the alternative as a separate amount-concentration subclass. Identify Rhodamine B, methylene blue, or another actual dye and initial versus time-dependent state; these dye names are not synonyms.
rationale: Dye concentration may be reported on mass or amount basis; the previous primary definition identified neither.  References 14, 17.
recommended_value: Mass of the identified dye divided by the volume of the prepared test solution.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents dye concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents dye concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents eis perturbation amplitude for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: For the described 2 mV peak-to-peak record, preserve voltage and peak-to-peak qualifiers. Do not hard-code 2 mV as part of the class definition or make every historical amplitude peak-to-peak. Consider alignment or subclassing with ACAmplitude.
rationale: This states the excitation quantity and convention while allowing a general EIS-amplitude concept.  References 34.
recommended_value: Magnitude of the sinusoidal electrical perturbation used to measure electrochemical impedance about an operating point, with voltage or current and peak, peak-to-peak, or root-mean-square convention explicitly identified.
registry_final_value: Magnitude of the sinusoidal electrical perturbation used to measure electrochemical impedance about an operating point, with voltage or current and peak, peak-to-peak, or root-mean-square convention explicitly identified.
released_value: An AC-amplitude characteristic specifying the small alternating voltage or current perturbation applied during electrochemical impedance spectroscopy.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents electrical percolation threshold volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Identify the conductive Pt/C phase, total-volume or solids-only denominator, transport direction, and fitted percolation equation. A finite experimental conductivity threshold must be reported with its criterion.
rationale: The threshold is a composition value marking onset of connectivity, rather than a geometrical extent.
recommended_value: Critical volume fraction of the specified conductive phase at which a system-spanning electronically conducting network forms in the stated material model or experimental system.
registry_final_value: Critical volume fraction of the specified conductive phase at which a system-spanning electronically conducting network forms in the stated material model or experimental system.
released_value: Critical volume fraction of the specified conductive phase at which a system-spanning electronically conducting network forms in the stated material model or experimental system.

current_value: A property denoting electrochemically active surface area normalized to Catalyst Mass and Pt Mass and determined in Cyclic Voltammetry, ECSABy Double Layer Capacitance, and Carbon Monoxide Stripping Voltammetry.
implementation: Use area units for this unnormalized quantity. Keep Pt-mass-specific area and total-catalyst-mass-specific area distinct, with explicit normalization-basis records or separate quantity classes. Do not assign area-per-mass values to an unnormalized area quantity. Identify the probe, charge or capacitance calibration, and conditions because accessible area depends on the probe.
rationale: Actual electrochemically active area and area normalized to platinum or total catalyst mass are distinct quantities.
recommended_value: Area of the catalyst surface that participates in a specified electrochemical probe reaction under the stated measurement conditions.
registry_final_value: Area of the catalyst surface that participates in a specified electrochemical probe reaction under the stated measurement conditions.
released_value: Area of the catalyst surface that participates in a specified electrochemical probe reaction under the stated measurement conditions.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents electrolyte concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use explicit subclasses or quantity-kind metadata for amount and mass concentration. Molality and mass fraction use different denominators and should be separately named. Identify analytical solute and avoid treating sulfuric acid, a generic dopant, and total ionic strength as the same observable.
rationale: A broad concentration concept can remain general if its value records state the concentration kind; an arbitrary molar basis must not be invented.  References 14.
recommended_value: Composition characteristic expressing the quantity of an identified dissolved electrolyte species per unit volume of the final solution, with amount, mass, or another declared volume-based concentration kind specified.
registry_final_value: Composition characteristic expressing the quantity of an identified dissolved electrolyte species per unit volume of the final solution, with amount, mass, or another declared volume-based concentration kind specified.
released_value: Composition characteristic expressing the quantity of an identified dissolved electrolyte species per unit volume of the final solution, with amount, mass, or another declared volume-based concentration kind specified.

current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents electron current for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Rename the preferred label to Electron beam current. Identify measured versus nominal probe current and acquisition mode as needed.
rationale: Electron-beam current is an instrument setting rather than an intrinsic electrochemical-interface property.
recommended_value: Magnitude of electric charge carried by the electron beam per unit time during electron-microscopy or tomography acquisition.
registry_final_value: Magnitude of electric charge carried by the electron beam per unit time during electron-microscopy or tomography acquisition.
released_value: Magnitude of electric charge carried by the electron beam per unit time during electron-microscopy or tomography acquisition.

current_value: A property denoting electronic conductivity anisotropy ratio.
implementation: Record the selected in-plane direction if the plane itself is anisotropic. The reciprocal TP/IP ratio requires a separate convention.
rationale: The IP/TP alias establishes the ratio direction; the replacement makes that direction explicit.
recommended_value: Electronic conductivity measured in the plane of a specimen divided by its electronic conductivity measured through the specimen thickness, for the same specimen state and measurement conditions.
registry_final_value: Electronic conductivity measured in the plane of a specimen divided by its electronic conductivity measured through the specimen thickness, for the same specimen state and measurement conditions.
released_value: Electronic conductivity measured in the plane of a specimen divided by its electronic conductivity measured through the specimen thickness, for the same specimen state and measurement conditions.

current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents electrospinning applied voltage for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Record the reference, typically ground, and the collector potential. Compute needle-minus-collector voltage only from commensurate signed potentials. The process is electrohydrodynamic rather than intrinsically electrochemical.
rationale: The source specifies needle voltage; it should not automatically be treated as the needle-to-collector potential difference when the collector is biased.
recommended_value: Electric potential applied to the electrospinning needle or spinneret relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.
registry_final_value: Electric potential applied to the electrospinning needle or spinneret relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.
released_value: Electric potential applied to the electrospinning needle or spinneret relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.

current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents electrospinning collector voltage for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State ground or another circuit reference and preserve the sign; do not describe the reference as an electrochemical reference electrode unless one is actually used.
rationale: A collector electrostatic bias is not an electrochemical electrode potential.
recommended_value: Electric potential of the electrospinning collector relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.
registry_final_value: Electric potential of the electrospinning collector relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.
released_value: Electric potential of the electrospinning collector relative to the explicitly specified electrical reference of the apparatus.

current_value: A transport characteristic that represents electrospinning ink flow rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm the source unit is volume/time before adopting. If it reports mass/time, use the alternative with a mass-flow label. Distinguish pump setting from measured jet throughput.
rationale: This is the usual volumetric feed quantity, but the source record explicitly leaves its reported basis unresolved.
recommended_value: Volume of polymer-containing spinning ink supplied through the electrospinning nozzle per unit time.
registry_final_value: A transport characteristic that represents electrospinning ink flow rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A transport characteristic that represents electrospinning ink flow rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: Equivalent radius representing the characteristic size of finite ionomer patches distributed over the secondary-pore surface.
implementation: Use this replacement only if the model uses area-equivalent circular patches. Confirm whether A is actual covered surface area or a projected area and how multiple patches are averaged. If the source uses a hemisphere, volume equivalence, or another model radius, retain that exact construction instead.
rationale: An equivalent radius requires a declared geometrical equivalence; the current definition does not specify one.
recommended_value: Radius of a circular patch having the same surface area as the finite ionomer patch represented in the model; for patch area A, the area-equivalent radius is sqrt(A/pi).
registry_final_value: Equivalent radius representing the characteristic size of finite ionomer patches distributed over the secondary-pore surface.
released_value: Equivalent radius representing the characteristic size of finite ionomer patches distributed over the secondary-pore surface.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents ethanol to water volume ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: This ratio differs from ethanol volume fraction; identify the pre-wetting solution or other mixture to which it applies.
rationale: The quantity describes formulation composition and has an explicit ethanol-to-water direction.
recommended_value: Volume of ethanol divided by volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture, with both component volumes measured before mixing under stated conditions.
registry_final_value: Volume of ethanol divided by volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture, with both component volumes measured before mixing under stated conditions.
released_value: Volume of ethanol divided by volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture, with both component volumes measured before mixing under stated conditions.

implementation: Exclude non-solvent solids. If the source divides by final measured mixture volume, preserve that volume-concentration convention explicitly instead of silently treating it as the pre-mixing-volume fraction.
rationale: The numerator and solvent-only denominator define a constituent fraction rather than a geometric size.  References 12, 22.
recommended_value: Volume of ethanol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.
registry_final_value: Volume of ethanol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.
released_value: Volume of ethanol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents ethylene glycol volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Name the other solvents and exclude dissolved solids from the solvent-only denominator. Preserve a final-mixture-volume convention separately if that is what the source actually measured.
rationale: The supplied description identifies a solvent-mixture volume fraction.  References 12, 22.
recommended_value: Volume of ethylene glycol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.
registry_final_value: Volume of ethylene glycol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.
released_value: Volume of ethylene glycol divided by the sum of the volumes of all solvent components before mixing, with component volumes evaluated at the same stated temperature.

current_value: A property denoting external quantum efficiency and determined in Review Statement Extraction and External Quantum Efficiency Measurement.
implementation: Use this replacement only for the photon-to-charge measurement. For a light-emitting device use the alternative as a separate subclass. For photon-driven chemical reactions, define the counted product events or transferred charges explicitly rather than reuse a detector definition.
rationale: Photoconversion and light emission use opposite photon/carrier roles; the intended device type is not fixed by the current text.
recommended_value: Ratio of the number of charge carriers collected by a photoconverting device to the number of photons incident on the device, evaluated at the specified wavelength or over a declared spectral band.
registry_final_value: A property denoting external quantum efficiency and determined in Review Statement Extraction and External Quantum Efficiency Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting external quantum efficiency and determined in Review Statement Extraction and External Quantum Efficiency Measurement.

implementation: Confirm the analytical method reports mass fraction before adopting. If only chromatographic area fraction is available, use the alternative and label it FAME chromatographic area fraction; do not convert it to mass content without a calibration.
rationale: A mass-based ester content differs from mole fraction and uncorrected chromatographic peak-area fraction.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents feed methane volume ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Use this definition and rename the preferred label Methane volume fraction in feed only if the denominator is total feed. If the source means methane-to-steam or methane-to-carbon-dioxide ratio, define that exact denominator in a distinct ratio class.

implementation: Rename the preferred label to Nozzle withdrawal speed or Syringe withdrawal speed, according to the source apparatus. Remove ink feeding rate as a synonym; define volumetric ink delivery separately.
rationale: The description denotes nozzle motion, whereas feed rate can also denote ink throughput.
recommended_value: Upward translational speed of the syringe or nozzle relative to the receiving substrate during formation of a printed pillar.
registry_final_value: Upward translational speed of the syringe or nozzle relative to the receiving substrate during formation of a printed pillar.

current_value: A property denoting estimated density of Fe–N4 sites from N 1s XPS fitting (assumption: 399.5 eV component originates from Fe–N4).

implementation: State which ferritin molecular assembly the reported amount counts. Keep ferritin mass concentration separate; do not assume an unreported molecular mass for conversions.

implementation: Record the precursor-mixture stage and volume reference conditions; do not substitute stock-solution concentration for final-mixture concentration.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents fiber ionomer to carbon ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Keep fiber ionomer distinct from any additional nonfibrous ionomer; state which carbon-containing support is included.
rationale: The source description resolves the ratio as a mass ratio.
recommended_value: Ratio of the dry mass of ionomer present as electrospun fibers to the mass of carbon support in the specified catalyst layer.

implementation: Use this definition if the reference domain includes the full catalyst layer, including pores. If the source uses only solid phases, use the alternative and preserve that basis explicitly.

recommended_value: Volume of the fiber-ionomer phase divided by the total volume of the specified catalyst-layer reference domain.
registry_final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents fiber ionomer volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A geometric characteristic that represents fiber ionomer volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: An electrochemical characteristic that represents fixed charge concentration in dry ionomer for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State the ionic-site species and ionomer acid or salt form. For multivalent sites, distinguish moles of sites from charge equivalents.
rationale: This is an amount concentration of ionic sites, not electrical charge per unit volume.
recommended_value: Amount of fixed ionic charge sites in an ionomer divided by the volume of the dry ionomer.
registry_final_value: Amount of fixed ionic charge sites in an ionomer divided by the volume of the dry ionomer.

implementation: Keep channel width, depth, number and hydraulic dimensions as separate characteristics.
rationale: The original labels an architecture category as quantitative.

registry_final_value: Categorical characteristic identifying the arrangement and connectivity of flow channels in a flow field, such as parallel, serpentine, or interdigitated architecture.
released_value: Categorical characteristic identifying the arrangement and connectivity of flow channels in a flow field, such as parallel, serpentine, or interdigitated architecture.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents free msa weight percent based on qd for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Before implementation, identify the chemical species abbreviated MSA and specify whether quantum-dot reference mass includes bound ligands. Do not infer the chemical expansion from the acronym alone.
rationale: This is a free-ligand-to-quantum-dot mass ratio, rather than a mass fraction of the final mixture.
recommended_value: Percentage mass ratio of unbound MSA ligand to quantum-dot material, calculated as 100 times the mass of free ligand divided by the stated quantum-dot reference mass.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents free msa weight percent based on qd for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents free msa weight percent based on qd for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents gas hourly space velocity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: For the existing mass-normalized data, preferably rename the label to “mass-normalized gas volumetric feed rate”. Reserve gas hourly space velocity for volumetric gas feed rate divided by catalyst-bed volume, usually h⁻¹; do not silently reinterpret existing numbers.
rationale: The contextual L gcat⁻¹ h⁻¹ identifies catalyst-mass normalization, whereas conventional GHSV often uses catalyst-bed volume.
recommended_value: Volumetric gas feed rate at specified reference temperature and pressure divided by the mass of catalyst used in the reactor.
registry_final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents gas hourly space velocity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents gas hourly space velocity for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A temporal characteristic that represents gel point time for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Record frequency, strain amplitude, temperature, illumination protocol and time-zero event. Do not generalize the G′ = G″ criterion to all gelation measurements.
rationale: The crossover is a protocol-dependent operational criterion and is not universally the true critical gel point.  References 55.
recommended_value: Elapsed time from the start of the specified curing protocol to the operational gelation criterion; for the stated rheological protocol, the criterion is the crossover at which storage modulus G′ equals loss modulus G″ at the selected oscillation frequency.
registry_final_value: Elapsed time from the start of the specified curing protocol to the operational gelation criterion; for the stated rheological protocol, the criterion is the crossover at which storage modulus G′ equals loss modulus G″ at the selected oscillation frequency.
released_value: Elapsed time from the start of the specified curing protocol to the operational gelation criterion; for the stated rheological protocol, the criterion is the crossover at which storage modulus G′ equals loss modulus G″ at the selected oscillation frequency.

current_value: A property denoting characteristic grain/crystallite size estimated from XRD using Scherrer formula (reported ~5 nm for β-SiC at 1600°C).
implementation: Use this definition only if retaining the GrainSize identity. The existing Scherrer-derived records should instead be assigned to a crystallite-domain-size class, whose definition is supplied as an alternative.
