released_value: A property denoting phenomenon/metric describing reduced ORR activity due to adsorption/poisoning of Pt by ionomer sulfonate groups (review discussion).

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents pt ru on carbon weight percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Keep the Pt/Ru atomic or mass ratio in a separate characteristic. If a source instead reports Pt-only content, map it to a separately defined Pt mass fraction.
rationale: The context identifies total metal content of the bimetallic catalyst.
recommended_value: The combined mass of platinum and ruthenium divided by the total dry mass of the PtRu/carbon supported catalyst, multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: The combined mass of platinum and ruthenium divided by the total dry mass of the PtRu/carbon supported catalyst, multiplied by 100.
released_value: The combined mass of platinum and ruthenium divided by the total dry mass of the PtRu/carbon supported catalyst, multiplied by 100.

current_value: A property denoting relative increase in mean current density per Pt surface (structure 1 reported 22% higher than structure 2).
implementation: Rename to relative increase in Pt-area-specific current. Multiply by 100 if expressed as percent; identify the potential and both structures. If Pt utilization is truly intended, use a separately defined accessible-Pt-area/physical-Pt-area metric.
rationale: The supplied observable is a relative change in area-specific current, not an accessible-Pt-area utilization fraction.
recommended_value: The difference between platinum-surface-area-specific current in a test structure and in a reference structure, divided by the platinum-surface-area-specific current in the reference structure under matched conditions.
registry_final_value: A property denoting relative increase in mean current density per Pt surface (structure 1 reported 22% higher than structure 2).
released_value: A property denoting relative increase in mean current density per Pt surface (structure 1 reported 22% higher than structure 2).

current_value: A property denoting description=Average power density delivered during a galvanostatic discharge pulse (energy/time over pulse).
implementation: This is a family definition, not permission to mix bases. Create/select a subclass for areal, volumetric or mass-specific pulse power and identify the denominator entity in every data record. If a single basis was intended by the source, narrow this class to that basis.
rationale: Restores the missing normalization required for any power-density quantity without guessing its basis.
recommended_value: The average electrical power delivered during a specified discharge pulse divided by an explicitly stated normalization area, volume or mass, with average pulse power equal to the energy delivered during the pulse divided by its duration.
registry_final_value: The average electrical power delivered during a specified discharge pulse divided by an explicitly stated normalization area, volume or mass, with average pulse power equal to the energy delivered during the pulse divided by its duration.
released_value: The average electrical power delivered during a specified discharge pulse divided by an explicitly stated normalization area, volume or mass, with average pulse power equal to the energy delivered during the pulse divided by its duration.

current_value: A property denoting quantum dot loading weight percent.
implementation: Use only if the source reports weight percent of the dry composite. If the reported denominator is host alone or wet ink, use the corresponding alternative and a label that states that basis.
rationale: A weight percentage needs an explicit material denominator.
recommended_value: The mass of quantum dots divided by the total dry mass of the composite containing them, multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: A property denoting quantum dot loading weight percent.
released_value: A property denoting quantum dot loading weight percent.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents ramp rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Prefer label temperature ramp rate; state signed dT/dt or positive heating/cooling magnitude and use the sample or programmed temperature consistently.
rationale: The description fixes this otherwise ambiguous ramp rate as thermal.
recommended_value: The rate of change of the heat-treatment temperature with elapsed time during a specified temperature-program segment.
registry_final_value: The rate of change of the heat-treatment temperature with elapsed time during a specified temperature-program segment.
released_value: The rate of change of the heat-treatment temperature with elapsed time during a specified temperature-program segment.

current_value: A layer thickness that represents reaction layer thickness fraction in mcl for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Identify sublayer Y and fraction/percent convention; use the same reference state and averaging convention for numerator and denominator.
rationale: Defines a geometric fraction rather than a thickness.
recommended_value: The through-plane thickness of the designated reaction sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the cathode multilayer catalyst layer.
registry_final_value: The through-plane thickness of the designated reaction sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the cathode multilayer catalyst layer.
released_value: The through-plane thickness of the designated reaction sublayer divided by the total through-plane thickness of the cathode multilayer catalyst layer.

current_value: A property denoting temperature at which reduction of a specific oxide (or binder removal step) initiates under given atmosphere and heating rate.
implementation: Define the onset criterion, reducing-gas composition and heating rate; move non-reductive binder removal to a separate characteristic.
rationale: Binder removal is not necessarily a reduction reaction.
recommended_value: The temperature at which reduction of a specified reducible species first satisfies the stated detection criterion during a defined atmosphere and heating protocol.
registry_final_value: The temperature at which reduction of a specified reducible species first satisfies the stated detection criterion during a defined atmosphere and heating protocol.
released_value: The temperature at which reduction of a specified reducible species first satisfies the stated detection criterion during a defined atmosphere and heating protocol.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents reference concentration for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: For the PEMFC CFD application, record the species, phase, concentration basis, reference temperature/pressure and the equation in which this value is used. Distinct physical reference concentrations may be modeled as subclasses.
rationale: Clarifies the role of a reference concentration without inventing the model species or reference state.
recommended_value: The concentration assigned to an identified chemical species in a specified phase at the reference state of a defined kinetic or transport model.
registry_final_value: The concentration assigned to an identified chemical species in a specified phase at the reference state of a defined kinetic or transport model.
released_value: The concentration assigned to an identified chemical species in a specified phase at the reference state of a defined kinetic or transport model.

current_value: A property denoting relative performance variation percent and determined in Fuel Cell Polarization Measurement.
implementation: Identify the observable (for example current at a stated voltage, voltage at stated current or peak areal power), test and reference states, and whether the formula is signed relative change, absolute deviation or a symmetric percent difference. Then define the exact numerator and denominator; do not choose peak power without source evidence.
rationale: The performance observable and comparison convention cannot be recovered from the supplied record.
registry_final_value: A property denoting relative performance variation percent and determined in Fuel Cell Polarization Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting relative performance variation percent and determined in Fuel Cell Polarization Measurement.

current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity coefficient low ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Adopt only after attaching source Eq. 7 and defining relative conductivity, R_I/C, the mass basis of R_I/C, the low-ratio domain and the volume-fraction normalization. Do not insert 2.3 as a universal constant or reconstruct the absent equation.
rationale: The contextual record identifies the coefficient role and branch but omits them from the primary definition.
recommended_value: The multiplicative prefactor in the low-ionomer-to-carbon-ratio branch of the specified correlation for relative proton conductivity.
registry_final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity coefficient low ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity coefficient low ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric high for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Attach the complete source correlation, define the R_I/C mass basis and branch threshold, and check whether a shifted ratio rather than R_I/C itself appears in the power before adopting.
rationale: The contextual record identifies which variable is exponentiated and the applicable branch.
recommended_value: The exponent applied to the ionomer-to-carbon ratio in the high-ratio branch of the specified relative-proton-conductivity correlation.
registry_final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric high for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric high for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric low for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Attach source Eq. 7, define the R_I/C mass basis and low-ratio regime, and verify the powered expression before adopting.
rationale: The contextual record identifies the exponent role but the primary definition omits it.
recommended_value: The exponent applied to the ionomer-to-carbon ratio in the low-ratio branch of the specified relative-proton-conductivity correlation.
registry_final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric low for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent ric low for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent vcb for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Attach the full source equation and define whether carbon volume fraction is referenced to the entire layer, solid phase or another volume. Check applicability in both correlation branches.
rationale: The contextual record identifies the powered variable without requiring a guessed numerical exponent.
recommended_value: The exponent applied to the carbon volume fraction in the specified correlation for relative proton conductivity.
registry_final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent vcb for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity exponent vcb for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity threshold ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Attach the source correlation, define the R_I/C mass basis and morphology assumptions, and state which branch includes equality. Do not equate this empirical boundary with a universal physical percolation threshold.
rationale: The contextual record identifies a branch boundary rather than a generic unspecified threshold.
recommended_value: The ionomer-to-carbon ratio at the boundary between the low-ratio and high-ratio branches of a specified relative-proton-conductivity correlation.
registry_final_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity threshold ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A transport characteristic that represents relative proton conductivity threshold ric for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A property denoting relative volatilization rate and determined in Solvent Property Measurement.
implementation: Record the reference liquid, rate basis and temperature, airflow, humidity and exposed-geometry conditions. The numerical reference need not be 1 unless that convention is used.
rationale: A relative rate requires an identified reference rate.
recommended_value: The volatilization rate of a specified liquid divided by that of an identified reference liquid measured under the same protocol and environmental conditions.
registry_final_value: The volatilization rate of a specified liquid divided by that of an identified reference liquid measured under the same protocol and environmental conditions.
released_value: The volatilization rate of a specified liquid divided by that of an identified reference liquid measured under the same protocol and environmental conditions.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents residual rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Retrieve the ink-stability assay formula: identify the retained/suspended phase or signal, numerator, initial/reference denominator, sampling height and storage time. Rename to residual fraction if it is a dimensionless retention ratio; reserve rate for a time derivative.
rationale: The record does not identify whether the value is a retained mass fraction, optical-signal fraction or temporal rate.
registry_final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents residual rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents residual rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents rheological percolation threshold volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Define the total-mixture volume basis and the onset criterion, such as an explicitly fitted modulus-scaling threshold; do not assume that a G-prime/G-double-prime crossover always defines percolation.
rationale: Identifies the compositional control variable and the operational onset.
recommended_value: The volume fraction of the specified dispersed-solid phase at which a connected structure first satisfies the stated rheological percolation criterion.
registry_final_value: The volume fraction of the specified dispersed-solid phase at which a connected structure first satisfies the stated rheological percolation criterion.
released_value: The volume fraction of the specified dispersed-solid phase at which a connected structure first satisfies the stated rheological percolation criterion.

current_value: A property denoting roughness factor and determined in Cyclic Voltammetry and Optical Microscopy Imaging Measurement.
implementation: Adopt only for the CV-derived electrochemical roughness factor. A microscopy-derived topographic real-area/projected-area ratio is a distinct measurement and should use the alternative. Remove inverse roughness factor as an alias.
rationale: Supplies a conventional electrochemical area-ratio meaning with an explicit numerator and denominator.
recommended_value: The electrochemically active surface area of the specified electrode material divided by the projected geometric electrode area.
registry_final_value: A property denoting roughness factor and determined in Cyclic Voltammetry and Optical Microscopy Imaging Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting roughness factor and determined in Cyclic Voltammetry and Optical Microscopy Imaging Measurement.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents saturated ionomer water content lambda for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State the ionomer equivalent weight and counterion state and whether saturation is equilibrium with liquid water, ice or saturated water vapor; this is especially important below 0 degrees Celsius.
rationale: Defines lambda using its conventional water-to-site amount ratio.
recommended_value: The number of moles of water per mole of ion-exchange sites in an ionomer at the specified water-saturation equilibrium and temperature.
registry_final_value: The number of moles of water per mole of ion-exchange sites in an ionomer at the specified water-saturation equilibrium and temperature.
released_value: The number of moles of water per mole of ion-exchange sites in an ionomer at the specified water-saturation equilibrium and temperature.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent a for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Attach source Eq. 5 and specify how G0-prime, phi and the fitted concentration interval are determined; do not transfer A between models without checking the relation.
rationale: The source description supplies the defining proportionality.
recommended_value: The exponent A describing the dependence of plateau storage modulus G0-prime on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation G0-prime proportional to phi raised to A in the specified rheological regime.
registry_final_value: The exponent A describing the dependence of plateau storage modulus G0-prime on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation G0-prime proportional to phi raised to A in the specified rheological regime.
released_value: The exponent A describing the dependence of plateau storage modulus G0-prime on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation G0-prime proportional to phi raised to A in the specified rheological regime.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent b for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Attach source Eq. 6 and identify the operational characteristic-strain criterion and applicable concentration regime.
rationale: The source description supplies the defining proportionality.
recommended_value: The exponent B describing the dependence of the source-defined characteristic strain gamma0 on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation gamma0 proportional to phi raised to B.
registry_final_value: The exponent B describing the dependence of the source-defined characteristic strain gamma0 on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation gamma0 proportional to phi raised to B.
released_value: The exponent B describing the dependence of the source-defined characteristic strain gamma0 on dispersed-phase volume fraction phi through the scaling relation gamma0 proportional to phi raised to B.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent t for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm that Sigma denotes electrical conductivity in source Eq. 10; state the dispersed conductive-phase volume basis and fitted interval. If Sigma denotes another response, substitute that exact response before adopting.
rationale: The supplied equation identifies a percolation conductivity exponent.
recommended_value: The exponent of the excess conducting-phase volume fraction above the specified electrical percolation threshold in a stated power-law correlation for electrical conductivity.
registry_final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent t for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents scaling exponent t for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A count characteristic that represents screen mesh count for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Record threads per centimetre or threads per inch and warp/weft direction. If the source counts openings instead, change threads to openings explicitly; do not treat the two conventions as automatically identical.
rationale: Screen mesh count is conventionally a linear thread density.
recommended_value: The number of mesh threads counted along a specified unit length of a printing screen in a stated mesh direction.
registry_final_value: The number of mesh threads counted along a specified unit length of a printing screen in a stated mesh direction.
released_value: The number of mesh threads counted along a specified unit length of a printing screen in a stated mesh direction.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents screen volume for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Prefer label screen free volume per area; confirm the source meaning and numerical definition of BCM/cm2 before unit conversion, and distinguish mesh free volume from the actual transferred ink volume.
rationale: The description identifies volume per area rather than an absolute volume.
recommended_value: The free volume of a printing-screen mesh available for ink transfer divided by the projected screen area to which that volume refers.
registry_final_value: The free volume of a printing-screen mesh available for ink transfer divided by the projected screen area to which that volume refers.
released_value: The free volume of a printing-screen mesh available for ink transfer divided by the projected screen area to which that volume refers.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents si c fiber volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Adopt only if the source percentage uses wet formulation volume. If the source uses dry solids or final composite volume, choose the corresponding alternative and narrow the label. Do not merge percentages on different bases.
rationale: Defines one explicit constituent-fraction basis rather than leaving the denominator unspecified.
recommended_value: The volume occupied by silicon-carbide fibers divided by the total wet formulation volume, multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents si c fiber volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A geometric characteristic that represents si c fiber volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A temporal characteristic that represents simulation time step count for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Store the integration step duration separately; elapsed simulated time equals the sum of step durations, not necessarily the count times one fixed step when adaptive stepping is used.
rationale: Separates a discrete count from simulated duration.
recommended_value: The number of numerical integration time steps executed in a simulation run.
registry_final_value: The number of numerical integration time steps executed in a simulation run.
released_value: The number of numerical integration time steps executed in a simulation run.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents sliding window size for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Record sampling interval, missing-data handling and feature count separately; a count alone does not specify a physical window duration.
rationale: The source context identifies a discrete sequence length.
recommended_value: The number of consecutive past observations or time steps included in the input window of a specified sequence model.
registry_final_value: The number of consecutive past observations or time steps included in the input window of a specified sequence model.
released_value: The number of consecutive past observations or time steps included in the input window of a specified sequence model.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents smp 10 volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Adopt only after verifying that the source uses total wet formulation volume. Record the exact precursor product and whether volumes are summed dispensed-component volumes or measured final mixture volumes. If solvent-free volume is intended, use the alternative.
rationale: Defines a compositional percentage on one explicit basis.
recommended_value: The volume of the identified SMP10 precursor divided by the total wet formulation volume, multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: A geometric characteristic that represents smp 10 volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A geometric characteristic that represents smp 10 volume percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents solid content fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Adopt only if the source uses a mass basis. Define which components count as dry solids, including whether ionomer/binder is included and the drying criterion. For volume fraction, use the separately defined SolidLoadingVolumeFraction.
rationale: Gives the conventional gravimetric solids-content meaning and distinguishes it from solids volume fraction.
recommended_value: The total mass of dry solid constituents in an ink divided by the total mass of the wet ink.
registry_final_value: A composition characteristic that represents solid content fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A composition characteristic that represents solid content fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents solid loading volume fraction for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Record included solids, density assumptions and whether total ink volume is measured or calculated additively. Use a separately identified dry-composite fraction for a dry denominator.
rationale: Identifies the phase-volume numerator and mixture denominator.
recommended_value: The volume occupied by the specified solid constituents divided by the total volume of the wet ink formulation.
registry_final_value: The volume occupied by the specified solid constituents divided by the total volume of the wet ink formulation.
released_value: The volume occupied by the specified solid constituents divided by the total volume of the wet ink formulation.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents solvent evaporation rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Adopt only if the paper defines a solvent-loss mass fraction relative to initial sample mass. Then r = -(1/m0) dm_solvent/dt is positive for evaporation. If the denominator is initial solvent mass, use the alternative. If the reported quantity is d(current mass fraction)/dt, recover that exact equation rather than substituting this definition.
rationale: The contextual description identifies a mass-fraction loss rate, rather than an absolute mass-loss rate or evaporation flux.
recommended_value: The rate at which the mass of solvent remaining in the sample decreases, normalized by the initial sample mass.
registry_final_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents solvent evaporation rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
released_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents solvent evaporation rate for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.

current_value: A composition characteristic that represents solvent to carbon ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State which liquids count as solvents and whether water is included; exclude metal and ionomer from the carbon denominator. Prefer label solvent-to-carbon mass ratio.
rationale: The context establishes a solvent-to-carbon mass ratio.
recommended_value: The combined mass of the specified ink solvents divided by the mass of carbon support in the same catalyst-ink formulation.
registry_final_value: The combined mass of the specified ink solvents divided by the mass of carbon support in the same catalyst-ink formulation.
released_value: The combined mass of the specified ink solvents divided by the mass of carbon support in the same catalyst-ink formulation.

current_value: A geometric characteristic that represents solvent to water volume ratio for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: State solvent identity and dispensed-volume versus final-component-volume convention; do not treat this ratio as a solvent volume fraction.
rationale: Defines the numerator, denominator and volume basis.
recommended_value: The volume of the identified nonaqueous solvent divided by the volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture.
registry_final_value: The volume of the identified nonaqueous solvent divided by the volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture.
released_value: The volume of the identified nonaqueous solvent divided by the volume of water used to prepare the specified mixture.

current_value: A quantitative characteristic that represents sonication amplitude percent for a material, component, process, measurement, or hydrogen-electrochemical system.
implementation: Confirm the instrument documentation and amplitude convention. Remove percent-of-maximum-power aliases; report actual power/energy independently.
rationale: An amplitude setting is not a percentage of acoustic or electrical power.  References 35, 36.
recommended_value: The sonotrode oscillation-amplitude setting expressed as a percentage of the maximum amplitude specified for the selected ultrasonic processor, probe and operating configuration.
registry_final_value: The sonotrode oscillation-amplitude setting expressed as a percentage of the maximum amplitude specified for the selected ultrasonic processor, probe and operating configuration.
released_value: The sonotrode oscillation-amplitude setting expressed as a percentage of the maximum amplitude specified for the selected ultrasonic processor, probe and operating configuration.

current_value: A property denoting specific activity.
implementation: Adopt for area-specific electrocatalytic activity. Identify reaction, potential/reference electrode, catalyst/ECSA material, current corrections and test conditions. If a source uses another meaning of specific activity, define a separate, explicitly normalized class.
rationale: Provides the conventional electrochemical area-specific activity meaning, distinct from mass activity.
recommended_value: The kinetic current for a specified electrocatalytic reaction divided by the electrochemically active surface area of the catalyst under stated measurement conditions.
registry_final_value: A property denoting specific activity.
released_value: A property denoting specific activity.

current_value: A property denoting dimensionless coverage inferred by normalizing CO displacement charge at 0.4 Vcell to ECA.
implementation: For the CO-displacement inference, document the background-corrected sulfonate-associated displacement charge, accessible Pt area, adsorption stoichiometry and full-coverage calibration charge density. Only then use theta = Q_displacement/(A_Pt q_full); do not claim that Q/A alone is dimensionless coverage.
rationale: Defines a dimensionless site occupancy rather than charge per area.
recommended_value: The fraction of the specified platinum adsorption sites occupied by sulfonate species under stated electrode and electrolyte conditions.
registry_final_value: The fraction of the specified platinum adsorption sites occupied by sulfonate species under stated electrode and electrolyte conditions.
released_value: The fraction of the specified platinum adsorption sites occupied by sulfonate species under stated electrode and electrolyte conditions.

current_value: A property denoting fractional swelling (dimensionless) of thin films as a function of RH and dopant concentration.
implementation: Adopt only if the source reports thickness swelling; define (h - h_ref)/h_ref. If it reports volume swelling, use the alternative. If a swollen/reference ratio is reported, use h/h_ref and rename accordingly. State humidity, temperature, dopant and reference state.
rationale: Gives a precise thin-film swelling observable rather than combining length, volume and uptake changes.
recommended_value: The change in film thickness on exposure to the specified environment divided by the film thickness in the stated reference condition.
registry_final_value: A property denoting fractional swelling (dimensionless) of thin films as a function of RH and dopant concentration.
released_value: A property denoting fractional swelling (dimensionless) of thin films as a function of RH and dopant concentration.

current_value: A property denoting tack value and determined in Rheology Measurement.
implementation: Retrieve the tack instrument model and protocol defining U.T., including whether the reported value is peak separation force, work of detachment or a calibrated empirical scale. State contact geometry, dwell time and separation rate. Do not convert U.T. to SI force without its calibration.
rationale: The instrument-unit value does not identify a universal force or work observable.
registry_final_value: A property denoting tack value and determined in Rheology Measurement.
released_value: A property denoting tack value and determined in Rheology Measurement.

current_value: A property denoting percent difference between thickness estimates from different methods/simulations.
implementation: Adopt only for signed reference-relative difference, 100(h_test - h_ref)/h_ref. If the source uses absolute or symmetric difference, use the corresponding alternative, and identify both methods.
rationale: A percent difference requires an explicit denominator and sign convention.
recommended_value: The difference between a test thickness estimate and a reference thickness estimate divided by the reference estimate, multiplied by 100.
registry_final_value: A property denoting percent difference between thickness estimates from different methods/simulations.
released_value: A property denoting percent difference between thickness estimates from different methods/simulations.
